newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE CELULOSA SELLS $19.8 MLN ASSETS.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE CELULOSA SELLS $19.8 MLN ASSETS.

text.p: Argentine pulp and paper maker Celulosa Friday announced the sale of assets of its tissue producer Tissucel to KCK Tissue for $19.8 million.
KCK Tissue is controlled by the local subsidiary of Kimberly-Clark Corp and Celucat of Brazil's Klabin group.

Celulosa said it was selling all of the machinery, equipment and other fixed assets at its Bernal plant in Buenos Aires province and would also transfer all of Tissucel's personnel to KCK Tissue by September 15. After the transaction Tissucel will be left with debts of $4.0 million.

Celulosa said it would also sell to KCK Tissue the assets of another of its companies, Cartulinas Argentinas, for an undisclosed amount. This leaves Cartulinas Argentinas, which manufactures thin cardboard sheets, with a debt of $4.2 million.

Celulosa said the sales were part of its strategy to concentrate on its core business, the production of paper for printing and writing, and to disinvest in controlled companies whose activities are not competitive.
